query: Single-phase high-entropy alloys have difficulty achieving a satisfactory strength–ductility balance. Earlier work introduced the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with a uniform, fine lamellar structure to enable large-sized production and obtain good strength and plasticity, but its performance still falls short of industrial requirements. Its use in aircraft and spacecraft fasteners further requires stability under extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosion, while relevant creep and corrosion studies remain limited by sample-size and experimental-environment constraints. Given these limitations and design requirements, what single intervention could improve the alloy’s practical performance? Present one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, causal mechanism, predicted improvement over the starting material, boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a feasible experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Laser cladding a Y and Hf co-doped surface layer onto bulk AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA will form a protective, thermally stable coating that enhances the alloy’s resistance to high-temperature grain coarsening and hot corrosion, thereby improving its overall performance under extreme temperature fluctuations and long-term mechanical loading.
generation.material_initial_state: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with a uniform, fine lamellar structure.
generation.intervention: Apply a laser-cladded surface coating that incorporates Y and Hf co-doping.
generation.conditions: Exposure to high-temperature environments (approx. 900 °C) with corrosive molten salts (e.g., 75% Na2SO4 + 25% NaCl) as well as long-term mechanical loading at room temperature to simulate cyclic thermal fluctuations and creep conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: The Y and Hf dopants are expected to modify the microstructure of the cladded layer by promoting the formation of a thermally stable, adherent oxide scale and reducing grain growth during thermal exposure.
generation.mechanism: Y and Hf co-doping facilitates the formation of a protective oxide scale (potentially Y- and Hf-rich oxides) during high-temperature operation. This scale acts as a barrier to corrosive species and suppresses grain coarsening, thereby retaining the mechanical properties and integrity of the coating under extreme and cyclic thermal conditions.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the uncoated or standard EHEA surface, the YHf-doped coating will exhibit reduced grain growth after heat treatment, lower oxide scale spallation during hot corrosion, and more stable mechanical properties (strength and ductility) over long-term loading. Although the exact percentage improvement is uncertain, a statistically significant enhancement in high-temperature stability and corrosion resistance is anticipated.
generation.baseline: The unmodified AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA, which, despite a fine lamellar microstructure, exhibits grain coarsening and limited hot corrosion resistance under extreme conditions.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is valid under the assumption that laser cladding can reliably form a uniform YHf-doped coating on the EHEA substrate and that the testing environments (i.e., high temperature, molten salt exposure, and mechanical loading conditions) are representative of the severe in-service conditions for aircraft and spacecraft fasteners.
generation.uncertainty: The magnitude of the performance improvements (e.g., the exact percentage reduction in grain growth and spallation area) and the long-term adhesion and stability of the doped oxide scale under cyclic loading conditions remain to be fully quantified.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of coatings on identical AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA substrates: one set with laser-cladded Y and Hf co-doping and one set with standard laser-cladded EHEA coating (control). Subject both sets to a heat treatment at 900 °C for 10 hours and then expose them to a corrosive environment using a molten salt mixture of 75% Na2SO4 and 25% NaCl. In parallel, perform cyclic mechanical loading tests at room temperature to simulate long-term creep and thermal fluctuations.
measurements: Grain size and microstructural evolution using SEM/TEM before and after heat treatment.
Oxide scale spallation area and morphology using high-resolution imaging and image analysis after hot corrosion testing.
Mechanical performance metrics (e.g., yield strength, ductility via tensile testing, and hardness) before and after environmental exposure.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Y and Hf co-doped coating does not demonstrate statistically significant improvements in thermal stability (i.e., reduced grain growth), lower oxide scale spallation area, and better retention of mechanical properties compared to the control coating, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: AbstractBoth crack-free AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) and Y and Hf co-doping AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA (YHf-EHEA) coatings were prepared by laser cladding. The solidification microstructure, thermal stability, and hot corrosion performance of the coatings at 900 °C under 75% Na2SO4 + 25% NaCl molten salts were investigated. The experimental results showed that the structure of the as-deposited coatings consisted of FCC and BCC/B2 phases. After heat treatment, an Al-rich L12 phase was precipitated in the FCC phase of all coatings. The grain sizes of the EHEA and YHf-EHEA coatings after heat treatment at 900 °C for 10 h increased by 27.5% and 15.7%, respectively, compared to the as-deposited coatings. Meanwhile, after hot corrosion, the spallation areas of the YHf-EHEA and EHEA coatings accounted for 14.98% and 5.67% of the total surface area, respectively. reading.lever: Apply Y and Hf co-doping via laser cladding to form a protective, thermally stable coating on the bulk EHEA.
reading.why: Prior evidence shows that Y and Hf co-doping improves thermal and corrosion stability, directly addressing the EHEA’s limitations under extreme temperature fluctuations and long-term loading.
